key_facts: A purple-blue lace-like pattern on the legs, arms or trunk.
Slowed blood flow in the venous plexus around each skin ‘cone’: physiological in cold, or due to vessel blockage, hyperviscosity or vasculitis.
Decide: complete and fading (reassure) or broken and fixed (investigate: FBC, clotting, antiphospholipid antibodies, ANA, cryoglobulins, lipids).
Antiphospholipid syndrome, Sneddon syndrome (stroke), cholesterol emboli after angiography, PAN, calciphylaxis.

sections.title: Overview
blocks: A **violaceous, net-like mottling** of the skin, caused by reduced blood flow/deoxygenation at the edges of the cone-shaped skin segments supplied by single ascending dermal arterioles.

ul: **Livedo reticularis:** a **regular, complete, fine** net. Often physiological.
**Livedo racemosa:** **irregular, broken, branching** rings ("lightning bolt") that **persist when warm**. Always pathological.
**Cutis marmorata:** physiological cold-induced mottling (infants, young women) that **disappears on rewarming**.

sections.title: Pathophysiology and pathology
blocks: Each cone's centre is supplied by an ascending arteriole at the **dermal–subcutaneous junction**. The periphery (venous plexus) is least oxygenated. Anything that **slows arteriolar inflow** (spasm, occlusion, vasculitis), **raises blood viscosity** or **impairs venous outflow** dilates and deoxygenates the peripheral venous plexus → visible blue-violet net.

head: Mechanism
Causes
rows: **PAN / cutaneous PAN**, cryoglobulinaemic vasculitis, SLE/RA vasculitis, ANCA vasculitis

**Antiphospholipid syndrome** (± **Sneddon syndrome** — livedo racemosa + strokes), **cholesterol emboli** (after angiography/vascular surgery/anticoagulation — painful toes, eosinophilia, AKI), livedoid vasculopathy, **calciphylaxis** (renal failure), cryoglobulins/cryofibrinogen/cold agglutinins, thrombocythaemia/polycythaemia, DIC, hyperoxaluria, septic emboli
**Amantadine** (classic), catecholamines (noradrenaline, adrenaline), interferon, minocycline, bismuth, quinidine, cocaine/levamisole; **heparin/warfarin** (necrosis)
Intravascular lymphoma, hypothyroidism, CNS lesions, erythema ab igne (heat), endocarditis

sections.title: Clinical features
blocks: Legs, feet, buttocks, arms; pattern, persistence on warming, pain, ulceration (atrophie blanche/livedoid vasculopathy, calciphylaxis), nodules (PAN), and neurological symptoms (Sneddon).

sections.title: Diagnosis and investigations
blocks: Warm the limb (does it fade?). FBC, clotting, **APL antibodies (lupus anticoagulant, anticardiolipin, anti-β2GPI)**, ANA, ANCA, cryoglobulins, complement, hepatitis B/C, SPEP, U&E (calciphylaxis/cholesterol emboli), eosinophils, lipids. **Deep biopsy from the white centre** (or several biopsies) if pathological; MRI brain if neurological symptoms.

sections.title: Differential diagnoses
blocks: Erythema ab igne (reticulate pigmentation from heat — laptops, hot-water bottles), reticulate eruptions (confluent and reticulated papillomatosis, poikiloderma), port-wine stain/cutis marmorata telangiectatica congenita.

sections.title: Management

ul: Pathological: treat the cause (anticoagulation in APS; stop amantadine/vasopressors if possible; PAN treatment).
**Livedoid vasculopathy:** compression, antiplatelet/anticoagulant (e.g. rivaroxaban — specialist), pain control.

blocks: Recognition, drug review (amantadine, vasopressors), bloods and referral.

refer.t: New livedo racemosa with stroke, TIA, miscarriage or clots: test for **antiphospholipid syndrome**.
Painful purple toes and livedo after an arterial procedure: **cholesterol emboli**, urgent referral.

sections.title: Red flags and when to refer

ul: New livedo racemosa with stroke, TIA, miscarriage or clots: test for **antiphospholipid syndrome**.
Painful purple toes and livedo after an arterial procedure: **cholesterol emboli**, urgent referral.

blocks: Livedo **racemosa**, livedo with **ulcers/nodules/purpura**, livedo + neurological symptoms (stroke/TIA — Sneddon), new livedo after an arterial procedure (cholesterol emboli), in renal failure (calciphylaxis — urgent), or in pregnancy loss (APS).

pearls: "**Regular, complete and fades with warmth = reticularis (usually benign). Broken and persistent = racemosa — find the cause.**"
Ask about **amantadine** in Parkinson's patients with leg mottling and ankle oedema.
